title: Progressive GPU-queue Drift and Silent-dep Blackout Playbook
creator: Aisha Rahman
description:
Goal: Build and run a repeatable chaos experiment that exercises two realistic failure modes that often interact in production: (1) slow, progressive drift of request queueing inside a GPU pool (queue drift) which causes increasing tail latency and delayed token availability; and (2) a silent downstream dependency blackout (blackhole) where an ancillary service begins returning empty responses or hung TCP connections without explicit 5xx errors. This runbook will validate our SLO thresholds, exercise adaptive circuit hysteresis tuning, and verify load-shedding behavior and fallback routing across regions.

Scope: harness + scenario definitions, metrics and dashboards, automated report generator, playbook updates, and a follow-up patch that adjusts circuit hysteresis constants if needed. Non-goals: changes to client SDKs or public API semantics in this ticket; those will be subsequent work if behavioral changes are required.

Acceptance criteria: (1) A deterministic chaos scenario repo + runner that can reproduce the experiment in staging; (2) Dashboard with p50/p95/p99 latency, error budget burn, token drop rate, shedding rate, and cross-region failover events; (3) Automated summary report after each run with SLO violation windows and suggested hysteresis parameter deltas; (4) Runbook entry in Confluence with step-by-step mitigation and rollback; (5) One rehearsal in staging with annotated results and action items.
steps: Design: define two-phase fault injection: phase A (queue-drift ramp) and phase B (dependency blackhole).
Infra: extend chaos-agent to support per-host queue rate-limiter perturbation and simulated TCP hang for dependency endpoint.
Instrumentation: ensure sampling includes KV-cache hit ratio, inflight request queue length, per-GPU scheduling latency, and downstream RPC histograms.
Experiment: run progressive ramp: 0-30min ramp to 60% effective queue wait increase; then toggle blackhole for 5-15min windows across a subset of control-plane neighbors.
Observe: monitor SLOs, circuit state transitions, shedding decisions, and cross-region routing fallbacks.
Report: generate auto-report with timeline, graphs, root-cause hypothesis, and remediation steps.
Tuning: if circuit hysteresis causes oscillation, propose new hysteresis constants and run A/B simulation to validate stability.
acceptance_criteria: Chaos runner and scenario committed to infra/chaos with README and reproducibility steps.
Dashboards and alerting for SLO regression visible in Console-staging and linked in PR.
Automated report produced after run with explicit windows where SLOs tripped and why.
Runbook page created and linked with clear mitigation and escalation steps.
Follow-up ticket created for any code changes to circuit breaker or shedding logic.
comments: 2026-02-25 Aisha Rahman: Created ticket to capture runbook and harness requirements. Initial scope sketched during reliability guild meeting.
2026-02-27 Diego Martinez: Design review notes - prefer incremental ramp to avoid tripping global circuit; recommend toggling blackhole on a small percentage (5-10%) of dependency clients first.
2026-03-02 SRE team (Lia Chen): Implemented new chaos-agent hook for per-host queue-manipulation. Pushed branch infra/chaos/queue-drift.
2026-03-05 Diego Martinez: Added instrumentation checklist; flagged need for KV-cache latency tag to correlate cold-cache events with queue drift.

2026-03-09 Diego Martinez: First staging rehearsal run completed. Observations: p95 spiked from 120ms -> 820ms during peak drift; circuit tripped on region-secondary after 12m causing shedding; cross-region fallback took 18s to fully ramp. No customer-facing 5xx observed but increased preemptive shedding affected 3% of requests. Attached run logs to PR.

2026-03-10 Aisha Rahman: Post-run retro - two action items: lower circuit hysteresis to reduce fallback latency and add a short-term grace window for small oscillations to prevent oscillatory shedding.
2026-03-11 Diego Martinez: Draft PR opened with new hysteresis constants and automated A/B harness. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving/pull/2241
2026-03-12 SRE (Lia Chen): Second run queued; adding dashboard annotations to capture exact timestamps for follow-up correlation with dependency logs.
notes: This ticket intentionally avoids modifying customer-facing API. The focus is on internal serving runtime behavior and circuit/shed tuning. If the experiment surfaces dangerous behavior (widespread customer errors), abort and escalate per incident playbook.
